Operator question 2026-10-16: make review faster but still safe as the code grows. Proposal (needs operator confirmation as a decision, amending D-gate-economy): per-item reviews see only the change's relevant hunks (DX-review-exclude drops generated/pinned files, DX-review-manifest gives each chunk the whole-change manifest) and risk tiers set the depth (tier:fast items get one combined review round, security/engine/hook globs keep the full two-reviewer pipeline; reviewer rules and tier floors are never relaxed: see GV-guardrails). A PHASE-END GLOBAL REVIEW runs as a periodic pass: one cross-family review of the phase's net diff (all merged items) on a large-context reviewer (the 1M-context LAN models), recorded as a periodic pass like integration_tests and required by the phase acceptance task (reuse DX-phase-acceptance-full-suite's hook; knob [review].phase_review = off|require|run). Measured 2026-10-16 (benchmark in /tmp scratch, repeat before deciding): runaway reasoning to the token cap, not diff size, is the main latency on the LAN DeepSeek models, so hedging and smaller chunks stay on.

CONFIRMED by the operator 2026-10-17 as decision D-phase-review (read it first); it governs this task and DX-review-exclude, DX-review-manifest, DX-review-delta-superseded.

Evidence 2026-10-16 (and earlier): committing a rule file plus DDFLOW.md needed the 'chore pattern' each time: create a chore task, claim it, copy the files into the worktree, commit, remove the primary's untracked copy, skip gates with reasons, merge, abandon: about 10 commands and several hundred tokens per use, done at least five times. Wanted: one command that does it, records the task, skips only the gates a chore may skip (configurable list, with reasons recorded), refuses code changes (globs outside a configured chore list: rules/, DDFLOW.md, docs/ddflow/decisions/ ...), and cleans the primary copy. Relates to the generated-views commit policy and DX-registry-files-shared.

GOVERNED by decision D-chore-class (operator 2026-10-17): configured chore globs; the chore completes without a reviewer, with skipped gates, reason and standing approval recorded; code changes always refused. This also fixes `ddflow complete` for a chore (today it refuses: 'no reviewer ran').

chunk_findings.detail:
The new branch keys only off `o["item"] == item` and never compares `o["holder"]` with the claiming identity (`log.agent_id`). The added comment asserts "another agent holds it", but nothing in the code establishes that. The exact input from the folded-in report — a wait entry `{"item": "T1", "holder": "u5pin"}` recorded while `u5pin` is the agent running the command — now renders

    Recorded: T1 is waiting for its lease held by u5pin.

which is still a self-wait: T1 is waiting on the lease T1 already holds, and the holder named is the claimer itself. The requirement was "either report 'already leased to you' or name the real holder"; the code satisfies neither for the same-agent case (the holder it names is not a real external holder, and it never emits "already leased to you"). Because `WG.register` persists this text/entry, every later reader sees a nonsensical self-dependency and cannot tell whether `u5pin` is the claimer or a third party. The fix rewrites the symptom instead of distinguishing the two cases the note called out.

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten message calls the takeover command an inspection: "Inspect it with `ddflow recover --item {item_id}`; to take it over, run `ddflow recover --item {item_id}; ...`". `recover --item` is not read-only — it is the state-changing step that must be run before the `--force` claim can succeed (the same message repeats it as the takeover step). A user who runs it believing it is an inspection has already mutated the lease/worktree. The one-liner is also joined with `;` rather than `&&`, so when `recover` fails (e.g. the crashed agent's worktree no longer exists), the shell still proceeds to `ddflow claim {item_id} --force`, forcing a takeover whose prerequisite recovery just failed — the opposite of the "exact next command" promise this change is supposed to deliver.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:316 (expired-lease refusal text)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's headline behaviour is untested: the intent says that when the EXPIRED lease belongs to the *same* agent identity, `claim` must renew it without `--force` (that is the three-command annoyance the task was filed for). The only expiry test in this file claims as agent "b" against agent "a"'s lease, i.e. the other-agent branch. Input that shows the gap: `DDFLOW_LEASE_TTL_S=1 claim T1 --no-worktree agent=a`, sleep past the TTL, then `claim T1 --no-worktree agent=a` — nothing here asserts exit code 0 on the renewal or the absence of the `ddflow recover --item T1; ddflow claim T1 --force` text, so a regression that keeps emitting the refusal/force sequence for the same identity (exactly the reported defect) passes this suite.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_claim_refusal_commands.py:56 (test_another_agents_expired_lease_names_the_one_line_takeover)

chunk_findings.detail: The folded DX-self-wait-wording item asks for either "already leased to you" or naming the real holder, and the reported wait record ("T1 is waiting for T1") comes from an item queued behind *itself*, i.e. the same agent re-claiming an item it already holds. This test only ever runs agent "b" against agent "a"'s lease and asserts the holder-naming sentence "waiting for its lease held by a"; the same-agent input (`claim T1 --no-worktree agent=a` while a holds/held the lease) is never issued, so the "already leased to you"/self-wait branch is unverified and the wording that produced the bug report can regress unnoticed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_claim_refusal_commands.py:25 (test_an_item_held_by_another_agent_is_not_waiting_for_itself)

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten refusal now prints the take-over sequence as "`ddflow recover --item {item_id}`, then `ddflow claim {item_id} --force`". Recorded project decision [D-lease-break-explicit] states that `[lease].break_on_timeout` defaults to false and that an idle, timed-out (i.e. expired) contended lease "is broken only by `ddflow claim --break`". So an expired lease from another agent is exactly the case the decision covers, and `--force` is not the documented break mechanism. Concrete failure: agent B sees "T1 has an EXPIRED lease from A ... To take it over: `ddflow recover --item T1`, then `ddflow claim T1 --force`", runs recover, runs the printed `ddflow claim T1 --force`, and with break_on_timeout still at its default false the lease is not broken and claim is refused again — the printed "next command" loops the user back to the same refusal instead of completing the take-over; the command the decision sanctions (`ddflow claim T1 --break`) is never shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:316

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal for "path already exists with <other branch> checked out, which does not carry {wt.branch}" now instructs the user to run `git worktree remove {wt.path}` as the unblocking step. This branch fires precisely when the path belongs to another item's checkout, i.e. a worktree that can hold that item's in-progress (modified/untracked) files; in that state `git worktree remove <path>` fails with "fatal: '<path>' contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it" and exits non-zero, so the printed command does not do what the message promises ("remove it, then `ddflow claim {item}` again"), and the user has no indication that `--force` is required. (The path is also interpolated unquoted, so a worktree path containing a space produces a broken command line as well.)

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement instruction drops the previous "move or remove it, or claim from a tree of your own" and offers a single command, `git worktree remove {wt.path}`, as the "exact next command". `git worktree remove` refuses to run when the target worktree contains modified or untracked files (it exits with `fatal: '<path>' contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it`), and the whole premise of this branch is that `wt.path` is some *other* agent's tree ("It is not {item}'s tree… with {there} checked out"), i.e. a tree likely to be dirty. chunk_findings.detail: The test pins the refusal instruction for taking over another agent's lease to `ddflow claim T1 --force`. data.decision: Operator 2026-10-17 (confirmed, amended by his answers). (1) PERIODIC ROADMAP REVIEW is a standard periodic pass of the default pipeline for every project (`roadmap_review`: by completed tasks, by days and at phase end). It prepares the data, runs read-only domain reviewers, validates their proposals mechanically (unknown ids, cycles, fix/DX edges to features, closed targets, 'do not abandon' stale cases) and then APPLIES the SAFE CLASSES BY DEFAULT: needs edges, priorities and glob narrowings above a confidence floor, always with a before-state snapshot, a recorded report and a rollback (`ddflow roadmap review rollback`). Merges, abandons, decision changes and anything touching a leased item are PROPOSED for the operator, never applied by the pass. A project or company can set the mode to `propose` (file everything for the operator) or `off`. (2) SELF-IMPROVEMENT LOOP: every agent self-monitors ddflow (rule r-ddflow-self-assessment, DX-auto-assessment) and turns bugs, missing features, misbehaviour and repeated manual work into proposals through ONE path (`ddflow improve`): duplicate-checked against the local queue, the roadmap and upstream first. With access to a ddflow source checkout (this repository or [upstream].source) it files into THAT repository's own queue through its normal verbs: never pushes, never opens a pull request, never edits ddflow code unless it claims a fix task there (D-upstream-reporting). Without a checkout it prepares a sanitized report and sends it to GitHub only with the operator's acceptance (B-upstream-surfaces). A GitHub workflow in the ddflow repository triages incoming reports (duplicate, needs-info, accepted, out-of-scope); accepted ones are imported into the ddflow queue as PROPOSED tasks. (3) KEEPING WORK ACTIVE: when a phase ends or the ready queue is empty ddflow may start, in this order, the periodic passes that are due (roadmap review, dedupe sweep, full tests), the phase retro, then the discovery research for the software the user builds; discovery only files capped, deduplicated, goal-linked PROPOSALS that the operator adopts, defers or rejects; it never creates work. The keep-busy policy and the discovery job are disabled by default, have a spend cap and the AP-kill switch. All passes are declared as data in config. This extends the goals-managed self product and project management (P-goals, P-autopilot): goals and key results drive discovery, adopted proposals become tasks, retros and the roadmap review feed goal progress.

data.decision:
A PACK is a shipped, versioned bundle of records (workflow templates, decision packs of D-decision-management, lesson/rule packs LP-*, skill packs, companions). Rules for all of them: (1) nothing is installed or enabled without the operator's consent (an agent may propose and run the dry run); (2) onboarding detects stack signals and OFFERS matching packs in the one onboarding conversation, with entry titles and counts; ddflow-usage and multi-agent-git are offered by default, never installed by default; (3) installed entries carry origin pack:<name>@<version> and trust=ddflow, are excluded from the project's own lesson/rule/decision counts and curate proposals until adopted (`packs adopt ENTRY` copies them), and are editable data; (4) an upgrade that changes a pack shows a diff and needs consent again; (5) per-entry effect (delivered, matched, repeated) stays in the project, never phoned home; entries never delivered or never matched are proposed for retirement; (6) pack entries are project-neutral: no ddflow-internal paths, ids or addresses (D-no-own-services-local-dir). Extends D-shared-engines-r2 (8).

OPERATOR AMENDMENT 2026-10-18: the ddflow-usage pack is installed by default when a project is bootstrapped (it describes how to use ddflow itself) and stays removable; every OTHER pack (multi-agent-git, testing, llm-review, general-design, workflow, decision, skill, companion packs) is only OFFERED and installed with consent.

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-18 (research /docs: history-collapse-extract): (1) GOAL: a smaller, tidier git history; the full ddflow history is preserved in the event log (which lives in the tip tree, D-log-in-main-tree) and in a verified archive. (2) ARCHIVE: before any collapse ddflow writes a verified `git bundle` of the repository plus .ddflow/blobs to an operator-chosen location, creates refs/archive/<date> and a tag in the local repository, and pushes nothing; release tags are re-pointed to their squashed equivalents and listed. (3) FORMS: whole range (single commit), per-phase or per-range squash, and the events-only squash of commits that touch only .ddflow, built in the first wave with an order-safety proof and a state-equivalence check. (4) AUTHORITY: operator-only (like `chore approve`: refused under an agent identity), CLI only (no MCP), with a dry-run plan first. (5) SAFETY: refused while other clones have unmerged shards, open pull requests, live leases or open worktrees exist (hard refusal, the operator may clear them); a `history.rewritten` event records the old-to-new sha alias map (blob), one `resolve_sha` serves every reader of a recorded sha, and `replay --verify-state` proves the folded state identical before and after. Nothing is pushed (D-fallback-no-remote); the command prints the force-push lines for the operator.
data.title: History collapse: smaller, tidier history; archive bundle plus local archive ref; whole-range, per-phase and events-only forms; operator-only; refused while others are affected

data.decision: Operator 2026-10-18: `regenerate a project from its ddflow records, ignoring the original source` means NEW IMPLEMENTATION AGAINST THE OLD TESTS: `ddflow extract` writes a self-contained bundle (manifest and digests, the records of every kind as JSONL, rendered docs, blobs, optionally an oracle pack of tests and fixtures taken from the tip tree), under a sensitivity ceiling and through the egress door (D-sensitivity); `ddflow seed` creates a new project from it: init, import the records with provenance in an imported layer, reopen every task as open, keep decisions, rules, lessons and research as records, and run seeded tasks through a pipeline variant whose oracle gate runs the old tests first. The queue, records and docs transfer mechanically; the source code does not (it is not in the log), and the command says so. Tasks need structured acceptance and oracle fields (SX-acceptance-field); a faithful verbatim clone of the ddflow data (`--mode faithful`) is a separate mode for moving history to another repository.

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-18 (merge-rebase workflow). Today ddflow only MERGES the base into a branch (DX-sync-command, 8f2d0547); [worktree].merge_strategy = ff-only needs the branch to already contain the base, ddflow never rebases for you. Add the rebase method: allowed only when (a) the caller holds the item's lease, (b) the branch is unpublished (not pushed, no open PR: ask the forge), (c) no other worktree or agent has the branch checked out, (d) no recorded merge or review round names its commits as a reviewed state we cannot remap. Before rewriting, record the old-to-new commit map (one event, branch.rebased, using the same alias machinery as HC-sha-readers/history.rewritten, resolve_sha) so recorded gate evidence that names the old shas still resolves; gate outcomes are keyed by TREE: a rebase onto a moved base changes the tree, so the recorded outcomes are reported stale (re-run required, correct), a rebase onto an unchanged base keeps the tree and the outcomes stay valid. Conflicts: abort the rebase (git rebase --abort), leave the branch as it was, name the files and the commits that conflict. Knobs: [sync].method (default merge, the strictest: rewrites nothing), [sync].rebase_requires_unpublished = true. Strategy presets (BR-strategy-data) choose the method per strategy (linear/github-flow projects rebase, gitflow merges).
data.title: `ddflow sync --rebase` and [sync].method = merge|rebase: bring the item's branch up to date by rebasing its own commits onto the recorded base, only when it is safe to rewrite them

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-18 (commit-rebase workflow). Agents leave many small commits (fix rounds, 'format', 'address review'). [worktree].merge_strategy = squash collapses them at merge, but only into one commit; a tidy step before review gives readable commits (one per logical change, a short message, no Co-Authored-By trailer) while the item is still unmerged. `ddflow commits tidy ITEM [--plan|--apply]`: plan lists the commits and the proposed grouping (fixup/squash targets by message, by files, by review-round markers; rules from [commits].tidy), apply rewrites ONLY the item's own commits above its branch point on an unpublished branch held by the caller (same safety checks as DX-sync-rebase), records branch.rebased with the old-to-new map, and asserts the resulting TREE is identical to the pre-tidy tree, so every gate outcome keyed by tree stays valid and nothing has to be re-run. A tree difference aborts and restores. Refused after merge, on a published branch, or when another agent holds the branch. CLI only (operator and the lease holder).
data.title: `ddflow commits tidy ITEM`: fixup and squash the item's own commits before merge (the commit-rebase workflow), with the evidence kept valid

data.body:
NOTE 2026-10-18 (RH-contradictions-2026-10-18, contradiction #28): A strategy is a NAMED PRESET over the existing [flow] knobs (github-flow = model trunk + integration pr; version-line = [flow.lines] + port_strategy; release-train = gitflow + cut cadence), declared as TOML data, so flow.model stays the single switch and the existing config/choices path records the choice (no third mechanism). core/flow.py and services/flow.py, ports.py already implement the substrate.

ORIGINAL TEXT (before RH-contradictions-2026-10-18):
A strategy declares, in TOML with a packaged default each: base per item class (feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, docs), merge target(s) and back-merge targets, branch naming, whether integration is merge or PR, how versions/tags are cut, which branches are protected, and the drift base. Built on the registry (P-extension-seams.registry). trunk and gitflow keep their behaviour exactly ([flow].model stays as an alias per D-compat); github-flow (short-lived branches from main, PR, deploy from main), version-line (long-lived release/x.y with backports and forward merges), release-train (periodic cut from develop) are added; an operator-written strategy drops into .ddflow/conf.d/. Per project, per line, per phase override. (Operator 2026-10-17, D-item-base-branch.)



MERGE/SYNC METHOD (operator question 2026-10-18): a strategy preset also names the merge method ([worktree].merge_strategy: no-ff | ff-only | squash) and the sync method ([sync].method: merge | rebase, DX-sync-rebase), so: github-flow = squash + rebase; gitflow = no-ff + merge; linear trunk = ff-only + rebase; version-line = no-ff + merge. The rebase methods require the safety checks of DX-sync-rebase.
